scenes.heading: Rationalising the denominator
scenes.sub: Move the surd off the bottom
scenes.say: Six over root three is a real number, but it is awkward to use. Today you’ll learn to rewrite it with a whole number on the bottom.
scenes.caption: 6/√3 is a real number, but it is awkward to use. Today you’ll learn to rewrite it with a whole number on the bottom.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A price written as 6 ÷ 1.732 dollars is right but hard to read
scenes.science: Rewrite 6/√3 as 2√3: same value, easy to read
scenes.breaks: 1.732 is only an approximation to √3. Rationalising is exact: nothing is rounded.
scenes.say: Imagine a price written as six divided by one point seven three two dollars. It’s correct, but nobody can read it quickly. Rationalising keeps exactly the same value but moves the awkward surd out of the bottom.

scenes.heading: Multiply by √b over √b
parts: equals 1, so the value is unchanged
scenes.say: Multiply the top and bottom by root b. That is multiplying by one, so the value doesn’t change. And root b times root b is just b, so the bottom becomes a whole number.

scenes.heading: A c√b denominator
scenes.question: Rationalise the denominator of 5/(2√10).
scenes.say: Five over two root ten. Multiply top and bottom by root ten only. The top is five root ten. The bottom is two times ten, which is twenty. Then cancel: root ten over four.
scenes.caption: 5/(2√10). Multiply top and bottom by √10 only. Top: 5√10. Bottom: 2 × 10 = 20. Cancel: √10/4.

scenes.heading: Where these fractions come from
scenes.say: Here is a square with a diagonal of six centimetres. The two sides and the diagonal make a right-angled triangle, so s squared plus s squared is thirty-six. That gives s equals six over root two, which rationalises to three root two centimetres.
scenes.caption: A square with a 6 cm diagonal. s² + s² = 36, so s = 6/√2, which rationalises to 3√2 cm.

scenes.heading: Length from area
scenes.say: This rectangle has an area of ten and a width of root five. The length is ten over root five. Multiply top and bottom by root five to get ten root five over five, which is two root five centimetres.
scenes.caption: Area 10 cm², width √5 cm. Length = 10/√5 = 10√5/5 = 2√5 cm.

scenes.heading: Which multiplier?
scenes.say: If the bottom is just a surd, multiply by that surd over itself. If the bottom is a binomial like three minus root five, multiply by its conjugate, three plus root five. Then the bottom is nine minus five, which is four.

Recap. Multiply the top and the bottom by the same thing. A over root b becomes a root b over b. For c root b, use root b only. For binomials, use the conjugate. And cancel at the end. Now try the practice questions!
